en: The sampaguita, our national flower, blooms with small white petals and a strong sweet fragrance in local gardens.
The narra, the national tree, drops small yellow flowers and grows winged seed pods during the dry season.
The Philippine eagle, our national bird, displays a distinctive crest of dark brown feathers in its forest habitat.
Indigenous Ifugaos carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into steep mountain slopes, creating observable stepped fields for growing rice.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate house exteriors with colorful kiping, which are leaf-shaped rice wafers.
The Baguio Panagbenga Festival celebrates local flower blooms with giant floats completely covered in real, fresh blossoms.
T'boli weavers create observable geometric patterns on t'nalak cloth using natural dyes extracted from local forest plants.
Exiled in Dapitan, Jose Rizal collected and documented local specimens of insects, reptiles, and plants for science.
The carabao, our national animal, has wide hooves perfectly adapted for walking through muddy local rice paddies.
Marine scientist Angel Alcala established observable coral reef sanctuaries to protect local fish populations from destructive fishing.
The South Sea pearl, our national gem, forms inside giant oysters found in the clear waters of Palawan.
Farmers harvest abaca, our national fiber, by stripping the long leaf stalks of the native abaca plant.
